trial_name.source_excerpt: protocolSection.identificationModule.officialTitle: '...("ProDERM Study")' -- CT.gov's own acronym field holds "IIM" (Idiopathic Inflammatory Myopathies), but the trial is universally cited as "ProDERM" in its own official title, the FDA approval letter, and every publication (PMC7793357, NEJM); used the publication name over the registry acronym field for identifiability, matching how other atlas trials are keyed by their real public name.

official_title.value: Prospective, Double-blind, Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Phase III Study Evaluating Efficacy and Safety of Octagam 10% in Patients With Dermatomyositis ("ProDERM Study")

drug.source_excerpt: protocolSection.armsInterventionsModule.interventions[].name (curated; generic name per FDA label, brand in parens per atlas convention for formulation-specific products)

value.description: Subjects randomized to Octagam will receive 4 infusions of 2.0 g/kg Octagam 10% every 4 weeks during the blinded First Period (16 weeks). If confirmed deterioration (deterioration at 2 consecutive visits) during the First Period, subjects will be switched to the alternate treatment. After response assessment at Week 16, all subjects with no confirmed deterioration during the First Period will continue receiving 2.0 g/kg of Octagam 10% every 4 weeks during the subsequent 6-months open-label Extension Period. At Week 28, subjects who are stable on 2.0 g/kg Octagam 10% can be switched to 1.0 g/kg Octagam 10%, at the discretion of the investigator.

Subjects randomized to placebo will receive 4 infusions of placebo every 4 weeks during the blinded First Period (16 weeks). If confirmed deterioration (deterioration at 2 consecutive visits) during the First Period, subjects will be switched to Octagam 10%.

dosing_regimen.source_excerpt: resultsSection.participantFlowModule.groups[].description (arm descriptions); infusion-duration/rate detail (2-5 consecutive days per cycle, initial rate 1.0 mg/kg/min up to max 4.0 mg/kg/min for DM given thromboembolic risk, versus up to 12.0 mg/kg/min for the ITP indication) from FDA label Section 2.1 Dosage table.

severity_criteria.source_excerpt: Eligibility criteria (text) items 3-4: "Manual Muscle Testing-8 (MMT-8) score <142, with at least 2 other abnormal Core Set Measures (CSM) (Visual Analogue Scale [VAS] of patient global activity >=2 cm, physician's global disease activity >=2 cm, extra-muscular activity >=2 cm; at least one muscle enzyme >1.5 times upper limit of normal, Health Assessment Questionnaire >=0.25)." MMT-8 <142 was a required threshold; the remaining criteria (physician global VAS, HAQ-DI, patient global VAS, extra-muscular activity VAS, muscle enzyme elevation) formed an "at least 2 of 5 abnormal" requirement, not all independently mandatory -- this atlas's SCORE_CRITERION shape has no "any N of M" operator, so 2 representative CSM thresholds (physician global VAS, HAQ-DI) are recorded here as illustrative members of that 5-item set, not as independently-required criteria; the full 5-item CSM list and its 2016 ACR/EULAR Total Improvement Score composition is in molecule/endpoints source_excerpt fields. Diagnosis itself required the 2017 EULAR/ACR (VALOR-era language) / Bohan and Peter (ProDERM's own protocol language) classification criteria for definite or probable dermatomyositis -- a categorical diagnostic rule, not a numeric score, so not represented as a ScoreCriterion row.
severity_criteria.extracted_by: manual publication_extraction pass (PMC7793357 ProDERM protocol + CT.gov eligibilityModule); cycle18

multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: ProDERM statistical methods (PMC7793357): single primary endpoint (TIS >=20 at Week 16) tested at a two-sided alpha=0.05 via Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test comparing responder proportions (Octagam vs. placebo) -- no multiple-primary-endpoint gatekeeping procedure (unlike the AD trials' co-primary IGA+EASI-75 hierarchy); secondary endpoints were analyzed descriptively/via ANCOVA and Kaplan-Meier without formal Type-I-error allocation. Sample size: 94 evaluable patients planned for 80% power. Missing data: not imputed except last-observation-carried-forward for the Week-16 ANCOVA when values were missing due to early termination or treatment switch. Both intention-to-treat and per-protocol analysis sets were used.
multiplicity_control.extracted_by: manual publication_extraction pass (PMC7793357 ProDERM statistical methods); cycle18

primary_completion_date.source_excerpt: protocolSection.statusModule.primaryCompletionDateStruct.date (registry records this as identical to the overall completion date)

study_schedule.source_excerpt: ProDERM design (PMC7793357 + CT.gov resultsSection): First Period visits/infusions at Weeks 0, 4, 8, 12 with response assessment at Week 16 (primary endpoint); Core Set Measures and CDASI assessed at each visit plus Weeks 28 and 40; SF-36v2 at baseline, Week 16, and Week 40. Extension Period: 6-month open-label Octagam 10% with infusions every 4 weeks (last cycle starting Week 36) through a Week 40 final assessment, with an investigator-discretion dose reduction from 2.0 to 1.0 g/kg available from Week 28 onward for stable/improving subjects. Total trial duration 40 weeks; each infusion cycle comprised infusions given over 2-5 consecutive days.
study_schedule.extracted_by: manual publication_extraction pass (PMC7793357 ProDERM protocol); cycle18

value.rationale: Not a topical/systemic step-up rescue design (unlike the AD trials) -- this is a blinded treatment-switch ('escape') design: a subject meeting the deterioration definition on 2 consecutive visits was switched to the other blinded arm (placebo->Octagam or Octagam->alternate) while maintaining the blind, rather than receiving an added rescue medication.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: ProDERM deterioration/escape rules (PMC7793357): "Deterioration was considered confirmed if worsening was observed on 2 consecutive visits," defined as worsening of >=2 cm in Physician's Global Disease Activity (10 cm VAS) AND >=20% worsening in MMT-8; OR >=2 cm global extra-muscular activity worsening; OR >=30% worsening in any 3 of 5 Core Set Measures. At Week 8 or later, confirmed deterioration triggered a blinded switch to the other treatment arm; subjects on Octagam who confirmed deterioration between Week 8-16 were discontinued at the end of the First Period. Switched/rescued subjects were counted as non-responders on the primary Week-16 TIS analysis. This schema's RESCUE shape (topical-then-systemic step-up, as used for the AD trials) does not fit a blinded-crossover escape design; fields describing topical/systemic step-up are left null and the actual switch mechanism is recorded in `rationale` and `trigger_rules`/`flare_definition` as the closest structural fit.
rescue_therapy.extracted_by: manual publication_extraction pass (PMC7793357 ProDERM protocol); cycle18

serious_adverse_event_rate.source_excerpt: resultsSection.adverseEventsModule.eventGroups[].seriousNumAffected/seriousNumAtRisk. CT.gov reports only 2 event groups for this trial ('First Period Placebo', n=48, and 'Overall Period Octagam', n=95) rather than a clean parallel-arm comparison, because of the blinded-crossover/escape design (subjects on placebo who confirmed deterioration switched to Octagam and are folded into the Octagam group; nearly all First Period placebo subjects (46/48) went on to receive open-label Octagam in the Extension Period too) -- the SAE rate is not a like-for-like placebo-vs-active comparison the way the AD trials' rates are.

most_common_adverse_events.source_excerpt: resultsSection.adverseEventsModule.otherEvents[] (top 8 by highest single-arm incidence; frequencyThreshold=0, i.e. CT.gov lists every reported term -- this is a curated top-8 subset, not the full table). Same 2-group caveat as serious_adverse_event_rate: 'Overall Period Octagam' (n=95) includes placebo subjects who crossed over.
